sentences.text: Atoposaurus was an extinct crocodylomorph that notably lacked the bony back plates, or dorsal scutes, found in most of its relatives.
Individuals of this genus grew to a maximum length of just 17 centimeters.
The genus was first described by von Meyer in 1850.
Fossils representing two distinct species have been recovered from France and Germany.
It serves as the type genus for the family Atoposauridae.
These animals lived during the Late Jurassic period, specifically between 154.8 and 145.06 million years ago in the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
Some paleontologists suggest that Atoposaurus might be a juvenile form of the genus Alligatorellus.
